correctness.rationale: For every finite simple graph, fPO is exactly endpoint orientation; EF and EQX become positive recipient indegrees and balanced indegrees. The integrality-flow characterization uses every subset, confirmed by exhaustive small-n orientation enumeration. For fixed c above c*, uniform Chernoff bounds over small and macroscopic subsets and complements produce all cuts; below, a second-moment low-degree argument excludes every feasible orientation. The critical point is excluded. Tests are finite corroboration only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Graphical EF feasibility with no equitability is weaker; uniform small-set circulation is additional. Rigidity proves neither joint fair-allocation existence nor its global orientation capacity constraints. The 2026 article abstract treats different combinations or restrictions; full-text coverage remains a stated priority risk.

value.rationale: The combination of exact EF, up-to-any-good equitability and fractionally efficient allocation has a natural economic fairness motivation; a sharp density transition for sparse pair-eligible indivisible items is a meaningful structural phase diagram. The global orientation existence above the local degree threshold is necessary to show such coexistence; just citing a known degree cutoff would not suffice. The theorem is an exact all-order asymptotic statement, not a tiny parameter gain.
